title: Israeli brother and sister evacuated from Nepal after landslides — Jerusalem Post - UA.NEWS
description: Israeli brother and sister evacuated from Nepal after landslides — Jerusalem Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
Israeli brother and sister, 27-year-old Maya Lamdan and 21-year-old Nadav Lamdan, were evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu, Nepal, after being in the village of Samagaun in the Manaslu trekking region during heavy rains and landslides. This was reported by The Jerusalem Post.

According to Maya Lamdan, the travelers decided to stay in the village when they saw a rain front approaching rather than continue their route. She said they were without electricity and heating for about 12 hours while temperatures dropped below zero.

Danger at night

At night, Lamdan said, the rain intensified, and at about 3 a.m. someone knocked on the door of their room and warned them of a possible flood. People were asked to climb onto the roof. They later learned that two landslides had occurred nearby, while another three or four smaller ones took place during the day.

Lamdan said local residents ran from the village to the hills in panic, using headlamps. She, her brother and friends underwent examinations at a hospital in Kathmandu after the evacuation. According to her, all of them are physically healthy and safe, but psychological recovery will take time.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Help for other tourists

Five other Israelis were traveling with Maya, while at least 10 other Israeli citizens were in Samagaun during the bad weather. Lamdan said she knew of tourists who had remained in the area and were also receiving assistance.

The emergency assistance center of insurance company PassportCard said it was helping dozens of Israeli travelers in Nepal. The company had information on 17 insured tourists in the Annapurna region, 17 in the Manaslu area, four in the Tsum Valley and two in the Everest area. Four of them needed medical assistance, but according to the company, none was in a life-threatening condition.

Due to the bad weather, travel was restricted in many areas of Nepal, roads were blocked and trekking was suspended. Clal Insurance and Finance reported that three of its insured tourists had already been evacuated to Kathmandu, while another seven were being rescued and were awaiting transfer to Kathmandu and Pokhara.

title: Auction to raise funds for families of Latvians missing in Nepal - Baltic News Network
description: Auction to raise funds for families of Latvians missing in Nepal  Baltic News Network
publisher.title: Baltic News Network
full_article:
A month has passed since 33 Latvian residents went missing in Nepal. To provide practical support to their families during this difficult time, a charity campaign titled “Across the mountains – back to our loved ones” is being organised.

As part of the campaign, a charity exhibition and auction will open at the Spice shopping centre on the 13th of October. Alongside the physical exhibition, a virtual auction catalogue will also be available, allowing anyone interested to view the donated artworks and submit bids.

The campaign is being organised by Andris Taranda, brother of Agnese Fūrmane, who is among those missing in Nepal, together with Ieva Taranda and Māra Andersone-Freimame.

More than 30 artists have responded to the call to support the initiative, including Ieva Taranda, Elita Patmalniece, Kristīne Luīze Avotiņa and Sabīne Līva.

All proceeds from the auction will go entirely towards supporting the families of those missing in Nepal, the organisers say.

The closing event of the exhibition and auction will take place on the 1st of November,

when the total amount raised will also be announced.

As previously reported, on the 26th of August a glacier collapse triggered a flow of ice debris, causing water and mud to surge from a glacial lake and resulting in widespread destruction in Nepal and China. By the 3rd of September, the confirmed death toll had reached 1,252, while another 4,216 people were considered missing.

A large group of Latvian tourists organised by yoga enthusiasts from Yantra was also near the epicentre of the disaster, while a smaller number of Latvian tourists were in the disaster zone as part of a group organised by the local company Mighty Himalayan Trek.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is aware that three Latvian residents who were in the region at the time were not injured in the flood-triggered mudslide in Nepal, while 33 are currently considered missing.

title: Nepal avalanche kills at least 2, with search underway for 12 still missing - CBS News
description: Nepal avalanche kills at least 2, with search underway for 12 still missing  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
Rescue teams were searching on Monday for a dozen people hit by an avalanche that killed at least four others on a Nepalese mountain during severe weather. Another 10 people were rescued from Mount Himlung, a 23,380-foot peak in north-central Nepal, after the avalanche hit on Sunday.

All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals. The avalanche hit as people at a base camp prepared for foreign clients to arrive to climb the mountain during the autumn climbing season, which began this month.

Helicopters brought down the 10 rescued, while the remains of the two found dead on Sunday were airlifted to Kathmandu airport and transported to the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital. Rescuers said they recovered two more bodies Monday.

All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals, officials said. They were at base camp preparing for foreign clients to arrive and climb the peak during the autumn climbing season, which began this month, when they were swept away.

Mount Himlung, right, and Mount Kanguru are seen in a file photo in the Nepalese Himalayan Mountains. Getty/iStockphoto

Flooding and landslides were reported in the Manang district where the mountain is located over the weekend, caused by heavy rainfall, the district administration office said.

The avalanche came as the government issued warnings of severe weather all across the Himalayan nation.

Nepal's disaster management agency said 21 other people had been killed and five more were missing in different parts of the country between Thursday and Sunday.

Nepal is recovering from devastating flooding in August that swept away several villages, leaving more than 1,400 people dead and nearly 6,000 others missing.

In early September, two people were rescued 10 days after the floods hit the country. One man was rescued from a 738-foot hydropower tunnel , and a woman was found alive in a house in the town of Nuwakot.

After days of continuous rainfall, floods in the Narayani River swept away a tourist cruise ship on Sunday. Fortunately, no injuries or casualties were reported, and the cruise was tied to the riverbank when the moorings broke.

The vessel then crashed into a pillar of the Narayani Bridge, which forced the authorities to stop traffic along the vital transit corridor. The incident occurred around 5:30 p.m. on Sunday when the Rhino Cruise, which was anchored 100 m upstream, broke loose due to floodwaters.

The unmanned vessel came downstream with the current and then struck the bridge pillar on the Gaindakot side. It posed a threat to the structure as water levels continued to rise, prompting the closure of all traffic on the bridge and causing great inconvenience to the residents.

The bridge connects Bhratpur in Chitwan with Gaindakot in Nawalpur, making it a vital part of the East-West Highway. Many vehicles, including freight trucks, are waiting in queues along the route for the water to recede and the ship to be removed to cross to the other side.

The Superintendent of Police Rameshwar Poudel said that the river’s current is strong, which has complicated the efforts to evaluate the structure. He added that traffic would remain suspended until teams can figure out and ensure the bridge’s stability and safely clear the hazard.

The water rise in the Narayani River was due to incessant rains, which have flooded nearby villages and forced people to evacuate their homes. Authorities and emergency response teams are on standby to assist in removing the ship once water levels recede.

KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescue teams on Monday searched for a dozen people swept away by an avalanche that killed at least four on a Nepalese mountain during severe weather.

Rescuers from the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, which is leading the efforts, said they recovered two more bodies on Monday in addition to two others who were found on Sunday. Twelve are missing.

Eight experienced mountain guides from the association took advantage of improving weather to dig through the snow that had covered tents at base camp.

Ten people were rescued from Mount Himlung, a 7,126-meter (23,380-foot) peak in north-central Nepal, after the avalanche hit on Sunday.

All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals. They were at base camp preparing for foreign clients to arrive and climb the peak during the Autumn climbing season that began this month, when they were swept away.

Helicopters brought down the remains to Kathmandu airport. Family and friends at a hospital morgue did not comment.

Flooding and landslides in the Manang district, where the mountain is located, were caused by heavy rainfall, the district administration office said. The avalanche had issued warnings for severe weather across the entire Himalayan nation.

Nepal’s disaster management agency said 21 other people have been killed and five more are missing in different parts of the country between Thursday and Sunday.

Nepal is recovering from devastating flooding in August that swept several villages, leaving more than 1,400 people dead and nearly 6,000 others missing.

title: Nepal Himlung Himal Avalanche: Four Bodies Recovered, Twelve Still Missing - News Mobile
description: Nepal Himlung Himal Avalanche: Four Bodies Recovered, Twelve Still Missing  News Mobile
publisher.title: News Mobile
full_article:
Kathmandu: Two more bodies were recovered on Monday from the site of an avalanche at Nepal’s Himlung Himal peak, taking the number of bodies found to four, officials said. Twelve people were still missing as search and rescue teams continued operations in the area.

The avalanche hit the base camp of the 7,126-metre Himlung Himal peak in the Nar Phu area of Manang district on Sunday. It buried a tent where climbers and support staff were taking shelter, leaving several workers and guides missing.

The bodies recovered on Monday were identified as Birendra Gurung and Ghan Shyam Rai, the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association (NNMGA) said in a social media post. The bodies of Chhebi Bhote and Pasang Bhote were recovered on Sunday, the association said, adding that its search and rescue team was continuing operations in the avalanche-hit area.

NNMGA President Tul Singh Gurung said the team planned to continue the search on Monday if weather and mountain conditions remained favourable, The Kathmandu Post reported. “Four bodies have been recovered and identified. Twelve people are still missing, and the search for them is continuing,” Gurung was quoted as saying by the newspaper.

According to the report, the search team led by Mingma G Sherpa of Imagine Nepal Trek and Expedition was flown by helicopter from Chame to the Himlung base camp on Monday morning to join the rescue operation. The bodies recovered on Sunday were flown from Chame Hospital to Kathmandu and taken to Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.

More than two dozen Nepali high-altitude workers and guides from Himalayan Holidays and Imagine Nepal Trek and Expedition had travelled from Kathmandu to Himlung about two weeks ago to prepare for the climbing season. They had been working on the climbing route and preparing the base camp.

The avalanche struck on Sunday amid continuous rain and snowfall in Nepal’s mountain districts, which have also triggered landslides and floods.

The deaths come as Nepal is still recovering from flash floods in August that swept through several villages, leaving more than 1,400 people dead and nearly 6,000 others missing.

title: Video: Screams Heard As Part Of Nepal Mountain Crumbles Into River In Seconds - ndtv.com
description: Video: Screams Heard As Part Of Nepal Mountain Crumbles Into River In Seconds  ndtv.com
publisher.title: ndtv.com
full_article:
In Nepal, two sets of videos from separate places have one thing in common -- each contains six seconds that are hard to watch. In that short time, a mountainside is seen giving way, and the people watching can be heard crying out as it happens.

The first video was shot near Lete in Mustang District, following a fresh spell of floods and landslides on Sunday. It shows a large section of a mountain sliding into the Kali Gandaki River in the valley below within about six seconds. Residents can be heard screaming as the debris rushes downhill. The footage was recorded by Char Dham pilgrims.

On Camera, Nepal Mountain Melts Into River In Seconds Amid Landslides pic.twitter.com/wzU4g2kout — NDTV (@ndtv) September 28, 2026

The river was briefly blocked by the debris before the water cut a path through and began flowing again.

In the second video, shot from a hillside, the ground can be seen giving way and sinking into the valley. Part of a stone-and-wood shelter and several trees are carried down with it. Villagers can be heard screaming as the camera pans, and voices shout "Ghar gai sakyo", which means "the home is already gone". A woman, probably a resident of a house on the steep slope, can be seen crying out in despair.

The latest floods and landslides have killed at least 24 people and left 14 missing across several districts. In Gandaki Province, the Kali Gandaki began rising on Saturday and had become a major flood by Sunday morning, following three days of continuous heavy rain.

The river caused damage from Mustang and Myagdi through Parbat and Syangja, and in one Parbat village it swept away an entire settlement. Landslides have also blocked highways leading to Chitwan and made search and rescue work harder, while security forces have moved thousands of people to safer ground.

Separately, two people were killed, and 10 others remain missing after an avalanche struck the base camp of Himlung Himal in Manang district on Sunday, police said. The avalanche hit the Nar Phu area of the 7,126-metre peak and buried a tent where nine climbers and 13 support staff had taken shelter.

These events come about a month after the Bhotekoshi floods, which struck on August 26. Authorities say that the flood has so far claimed more than 1,400 lives and left more than 6,000 people missing.

title: 10,000 Ancient Caves Cover the Cliffs of Nepal’s Mustang Region - Tomorrow's World Today
description: 10,000 Ancient Caves Cover the Cliffs of Nepal’s Mustang Region  Tomorrow's World Today
publisher.title: Tomorrow's World Today
full_article:
If you travel to the Mustang region of Nepal, you find yourself high up in the Himalayas. It is a harsh, dry, and windy landscape. But if you look closely at the steep, sandy cliffs rising above the Kali Gandaki River, you will see something strange. The rock walls are completely covered in small, dark holes.

Photo: Shutterstock/Wim Hoek

These are the Mustang Sky Caves. There are an estimated 10,000 of these caves clustered together in the rock. And they were not made by wind or rain. Humans carved every single one of them directly into the side of the cliffs. Some of the holes sit more than 150 feet above the valley floor.

Built High In The Rock

The cliff walls here are made of a soft, crumbly sandstone. Thousands of years ago, people figured out they could easily dig into the rock to create shelters. But getting up there was not easy. To reach the caves, they had to scale the sheer cliff faces or use ropes and long wooden ladders.

Photo: Shutterstock/Jasper Neupane

Archaeologists think the caves were used for several reasons over the years. Around 3,000 years ago, they started as burial chambers. Hundreds of years later, when violent conflicts broke out in the area, people actually moved their families into the caves to hide from invading armies. The high spots made it impossible for enemies to surprise them. They could pull their ladders up and wait it out.

Advertisement (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});

A Hidden Buddhist Center

Later on, the purpose of the caves changed again. By the 1400s, local people turned many of them into Buddhist monasteries and quiet meditation rooms.

Photo: Shutterstock/The Explorers From Nepal

Modern researchers have managed to climb into these high caves and found incredible things left behind. Some of the rooms are still covered in bright, painted murals showing Buddhist teachings. They also found thousands of ancient manuscripts hidden under the dust. Because the air up in the mountains is so dry and cold, the paper and paint stayed perfectly preserved for centuries.

Most of the caves are empty now. The wooden ladders rotted away a long time ago. This makes them incredibly difficult to reach today. But they still sit up on the cliffs, leaving a massive, artificial mystery right in the middle of the Himalayas.

title: Russian Ambassador to Nepal, Alexi, calls on Minister Pokharel - The Rising Nepal

full_article:
Kathmandu, Sept 28: Russia's Ambassador to Nepal, Alexi Vladimirovich Surovtsev, today paid a courtesy call on Minister for Education and Sports, Sasmit Pokharel.

In the meeting held at the Singha Durbar-based Ministry of Education and Sports, the two exchanged views on Nepal-Russia bilateral relations and mutual interests, according to the Minister's Secretariat.

Discussions were also held on the enhancement of mutual cooperation in education, sports, human resources development and other areas of mutual concern, it is said.

On the occasion, Minister Pokharel who also serves as the government's Spokesperson thanked the Government of Russia for its support and contribution to the human resource development in Nepal. He utilized the time to call for further expanding Nepal-Russia collaboration in the areas of education and sports.

The ambassador said that Russia is interested in investing in Nepal's education and sports sectors. He was of the opinion further exploring new areas of collaboration in these areas and further strengthening bilateral relations. (RSS)
